note: Measured values, not estimates. Regenerate with tests/corpus/README.md instructions if files change.

files.name: en_long_article.txt
tests: primary happy path for every carrier and cipher
confirms the ~40 percent substitutable ratio
long enough to carry a full 24-byte preamble plus payload
excerpt survival: any 160-char window should locate a resync marker

files.name: fr_accented.txt
tests: accented Latin must not break position counting or strip round-trip
NFC and NFD normalisation must not alter recovered payload
n-gram oracle must identify French, not English

files.name: technical_markdown.md
tests: structured text with code fences and tables survives round-trip
substitution inside a fenced code block would corrupt commands: verify placement policy
format survivability when exported to HTML and back

files.name: mixed_multilingual.txt
tests: n-gram oracle must report low confidence or multiple candidates, never a confident wrong answer
realistic distribution notice: the canary trap primary use case

files.name: en_short.txt
tests: below the 24-byte preamble threshold: standard mode must refuse, not truncate
detached signature mode is the only valid path here
n-gram scoring below the ~40 byte floor must report not-applicable

files.name: minimal_tiny.txt
tests: zero effective capacity: every carrier must raise CapacityExceeded
must never silently produce an unusable document

files.name: cjk_japanese.txt
tests: zero homoglyph capacity on non-Latin script: must raise, never fall back silently to another carrier
invisible-character carriers remain viable here: capacity should be non-zero for zero_width
demonstrates that carrier choice is script-dependent and the UI must say so

files.name: cyrillic_russian.txt
tests: DESTRUCTIVE TRAP: homoglyph strip() maps Cyrillic back to Latin, which would corrupt legitimate Russian text
strip() must be non-destructive on text that was never encoded, or be gated on prior detection
detect() sees Cyrillic without Latin so ScriptMix does not fire: verify no false positive
stealth mode salt derives from strip_all output, so a corrupting strip breaks salt reproducibility

files.name: already_carrying.txt
tests: contains U+200B, U+200C, U+2060 and U+FEFF before any encoding
detect() must not report a payload where none exists
encoding over pre-existing invisibles must not corrupt extraction
stealth mode: strip_all removes these, so the derived salt differs from a naive hash of the raw text
